start_here: Say to your AI: "Find how two of the person's records connect through relations and things that happened, or what several records all relate to and who else shares it", with {"of":["me"],"limit":1}. It runs tool:find-how-records-connect and answers {"of":["record:person:me"],"hubs":[],"members":[],"count":{"hubs":0,"members":0},"complete":true,"read":{"relations":0,"activities":0}}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and keeps only its own rows (relation, activity) through the records door.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Find how two of the person's records connect through relations and things that happened, or what several records all relate to and who else shares it", and give it nothing more: every input is optional.
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:find-how-records-connect and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: With from and to: the paths between them, shortest first, each at most max_length steps (default 4, at most 6), each step one relation or one record to an activity it took part in, with the relation or activity it goes through and the role.
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: relation (records:read, records:list); activity (records:read, records:list).
